real_vs_reconstructed_rng_finding.summary: CTaskInteriorSitAtDesk::ProcessPed's line `if (CGeneral::GetRandomNumber() < 0x3FFF)` calls the DLL's CGeneral::GetRandomNumber(), which forwards to the CRT's rand(). The original machine code at this exact call site inlines a direct call to the internal LCG at 0x821B1E (`seed = seed*0x343FD + 0x269EC3; (seed>>16)&0x7FFF`), the same generator the rest of the original EXE uses, bypassing CGeneral::GetRandomNumber's own address entirely. These are two independent random sequences even in real unmodified gameplay (a pre-existing, already-documented limitation of CGeneral::GetRandomNumber's reconstruction, see source/game_sa/General.cpp:200). To compare the SAME branch decision on both sides, the bank patches both CGeneral::GetRandomNumber (the DLL symbol) and the raw 0x821B1E entry to the same fixed per-pair value, matching the technique already used by reversing/CGeneral/LiveComparison.hpp.
real_vs_reconstructed_rng_finding.not_a_bug_in_task: ProcessPed's C++ correctly uses the project's standard RNG abstraction; the divergence is purely a consequence of General.cpp's already-documented RNG gap, not something specific to this function.

correction_the_stall_was_not_the_daemon_.what_actually_happened: The 'DaemonUpdateAssistant' crash-loop correlation above was misleading. The user manually stopped that service and verified it and any GTA process were gone, then asked for the 144-pair bank to be re-run as a regression check. It STILL stalled at 'waiting_for_player' with the service confirmed off. The real cause: run_local.py/run.py only check the installed probe's hash against PROBE_HASH and launch it -- they never call build_probe.py. The LiveComparison.hpp edit (removing the redundant InjectHooks() call) was never rebuilt or reinstalled into _baseline/gta_reversed-sitatdesk-probe.asi in the test copy, so every run in this session (including the two blamed on the Daemon service) was still executing the OLD probe binary (built 2026-10-01 15:49, i.e. still containing the duplicate-hook bug). That binary hits the CRT assertion dialog (HookCategory.h:60) every time, which is a MODAL dialog box -- it blocks the game's main thread entirely, so the probe's own code (including writing 'player_ready') never runs. That is exactly indistinguishable from a plain hang unless someone is watching the screen. The user caught this live, force-closed the stuck GTA process, and asked for the probe to actually be rebuilt.
